review:
For a buck or two, the game has some heart and theme. 

Pretty typical shmup, and the style fits Hentenko Doujin's style: crappy homebrew games with a game mechanic twist. So if you are looking for a "B" movie equivalent in video games, then you've found your publisher haha.

Now, having taken that low jab, I have to say this game is great in short stretches. 6 levels, 2-3 mins long each. 70% of the achievements are easy to acquire. The bullet hell always seems manageable, and what will get you killed is primarily losing track of where your hitbox actually is given how big the player sprite is. Since the player hitbox is off-center from the player sprite, often times you might lose track and get cross-eyed dodging correctly as most shmups center the hitbox in the sprite.

Personally, I enjoy short and sweet shmups. I can do the 30-45 minute ones, but my brain gets exhausted, plus, spending that long then making a couple critical mistakes at the True Last Boss,,,,oof,,, here all the bosses are more than fair and do not spend too long on your doormat trying to convert you to Jesus. 

Love the theme. If a Vulkaiser II came out I would be game for more short snippets of 70/80s anime character personalities. 

The switching in and out of Kaiser components does add a touch of strategy, and you will want to preserve your buddy components as much as possible not only for score, but simply to give them the time to heal, so you have them when you need them and they can take a few more hits for you down the road.

Aight, definite recommend on sale. Not deep, but it's sweet.

街机风格的清版射击游戏，一开始是冲着昭和机器人要素买的，这方面要素也确实齐全，特别是能看出来受了长滨忠夫作品的不少影响。邪恶的外星侵略者来袭，唯一能拯救地球的就是性格各异的五人战队驾驶的超级机器人；经典的火箭飞拳、风格各异的四种强化形态、以生物为原型设计的敌方机械、巨大的外星母舰、跟主角缠斗了一整个主线最后在惺惺相惜中落败，身为敌人却高贵矜持让人讨厌不起来的宿敌角色，以及到最后才登场的真正的黑幕boss，也都是昭和机器人常见的要素。这是属于几十年前那个时代的单纯明快的作品，可能不符合现在的主流审美，但是总有人就吃这一套。

动画和游戏的表现形式不一样，要用一局10分钟的街机模式去讲一部50多集TV动画该讲的完整故事，只能把大部分桥段都过滤掉，留下整个故事最精髓的部分。不熟悉昭和机器人常见的兴奋点的话要实现这样的浓缩是不可能的事情，换句话说制作组不仅很懂玩家要什么，也很懂怎么给——对有积累的玩家，不需要把所有情节都做出来端到他们嘴边，只要把关键点做到位，其他次要的部分完全可以交给玩家自己去想象。

除了剧情设定以外，游戏本身也是非常优秀的街机清版射击作品，主角萝卜的基础形态和其他四种形态平衡性做得很好，每种形态都有各自的战斗策略，而且敌人也不会太硬，清屏相当爽快。但难度上来以后也是街机级别的难，超难模式我一度怀疑是做给新人类玩的，比打黑魂的时候还绝望，慢慢参考着b站通关视频才打完。

I'm going to go with a very luke-warm recommend.  Robot Vulkaiser has a lot of charm in its premise, and it could have even done a better job capitalizing on that. You pilot a 1970s style anime giant robot with the special attack of thunderball fists.  During the level you'll get the chance to combine with another pilot module to change attack.  This ranges from missiles with an explosion attack, a rapid fire needle attack, a wide ranged thunder attack and a powerful close ranged drill attack.  However, each module has its own life bar, and when the module is destroyed you lose access to it for the remainder of your play through.

More than 3/4 of the enemy bullets fire at the place your giant robot is on screen. With some of the bigger enemies, mid-level bosses and end of level bosses having rudimentary bullet patterns.  And if it were not for the sheer volume of fire, the game would be fairly easy.  But that doesn't change that the game is rather shallow.  The location of you giant robot's actual hitbox takes some getting used to.  But the game is very clear to where it is located.

I'm mixed about the graphics.  As the game is clearly going for an 1970s Japanese cartoon style, but I also can't help to think the game was a little lazy about the graphical assets too.  The sound and music is good, if lacking in variety.  The game tries to frame levels as individual episodes, but doesn't go any further than that.  Which I find a shame, as Robot Vulkaiser could have been a lot of fun with some campy cut scenes at the start and end of levels.  Even if just still images.

Ultimately, Robot Vulkaiser is a simple and shallow, shmup with an interesting theme that should have been explored further.  It's fine as an extreme budget title, but could have been more if a little more polish and effort was put in.

일본의 인디 게임 개발사가 동인 게임 개발 서클 시절인 2007년에 만든 데뷔작을, 2015년에 스팀으로 출시한 작품. 

70년대 로봇 애니메이션 컨셉인 슈팅 게임으로, 게임적인 부분은 '아로마'에서 1999년에 PS1용으로 만든 '70년대풍 로봇 아니메 겟P-X'의 영향을 받은 듯싶다. 다만, 겟P-X가 겟타 로보의 오마쥬인 반면. 본작은 '초전기로보'라는 명칭부터가 '초전자로보 컴배틀러 V'의 오마쥬고, 무기 파츠 장착과 주인공 일행 파일럿 제복 디자인을 보면 '초인전대 바라타크'에 가깝다.

원작의 리마스터, 리부트, 리메이크 요소 없이 그대로 가지고 와서 윈도우창 모드의 화면 크기는 좀 작지만, 그래픽 자체는 깔끔한 편이다.

잔기 대신 내구력의 개념이 있어서 한 대 맞아도 죽지 않고. 총알의 자동 연사와 챠지 샷을 동시 지원해서 쾌적하다. 공격 키를 꾹 누르고 있으면 자동 연사를 하는데 파워 게이지도 함께 차올라서, 공격 키에서 손을 떼면 챠지 샷이 나가는 방식이라 공격의 템포가 끊이지 않아서 좋다.

무기의 파워업 개념은 없지만, 파츠 입수로 무기를 변경하면 처음부터 최대 화력을 낼 수 있고. 무기 파츠별 일반 샷, 챠지 샷, 폭탄이 달라져서 무기를 바꿔가며 플레이하는 맛이 있다.

캐릭터, 기체 디자인, 연출, 음악, 효과음 등. 게임 전반적인 부분에서 70년대 로봇 애니메이션 컨셉을 충실히 살리고 있어 복고풍의 매력이 넘친다. 레트로 컨셉의 인디 게임은 레트로 감성만 어필하지 게임성이 떨어지는 경우가 적지 않은데. 본작은 레트로 감성과 게임성이라는 두 마리의 토끼를 다 잡았다.

Supercharged Robot VULKAISER is a fast-paced, side-scrolling shooter that brings back that old-school arcade feel with modern polish. You pilot a giant robot packed with powerful weapons and abilities, blasting through waves of enemies and massive bosses in a relentless, adrenaline-fueled experience.

The gameplay is intense and satisfying, combining smooth controls with plenty of firepower and movement options. There’s a great sense of speed and impact, making every battle feel exciting and rewarding. Each level is packed with enemies and hazards that keep you on your toes, and the boss fights add a nice challenge that tests your skills without feeling unfair.

Visually, the game has a vibrant, retro-inspired style with detailed pixel art and effects that pop on screen. The soundtrack amps up the energy with high-octane tunes that perfectly match the action.

I recommend Supercharged Robot VULKAISER because it’s a fantastic pick for anyone who loves classic shooter gameplay with a modern twist. It’s challenging but fair, fast but controlled, and overall just a blast to play. Whether you’re into mechs, shooters, or just want something that delivers pure, unfiltered arcade action, this game hits the mark. 10/10

昭和末期の夕暮れ時、こういう'70アニメがちょこちょこ再放送されてまして。
本放送時、オヤジ世代が子供の頃熱中してたんだろうなー、と幼心にぼんやり眺めていたものです。
このゲームはそのオマージュ作品（OPからして当時の児童雑誌コンパチ）なのですが、STGとしての内容はコテコテのアーリー90年代、それもアッパー調整。
イージーでこそFC～PCE向けSTGライクな難易度ですが、ノーマル以上はかなり激しい内容です。
スーパーロボットを駆りサポートウィングと合体し高火力と切り札のボムを手に入れる’70様式美は、意外なほどオーソドックスSTGとマッチします。
そして、その設計思想が素晴らしい。被弾した時に本体だけではなくウィングも体力を削られ、ボムの補給も合体時のみという調整で、得意なウィングでひたすら回すより万遍なく使った方がお得。
これが、「結局XX装備でYYするだけなんだよなぁ」を回避する一助になっています（無論、そういう遊び方もできます。RTAでは合体アニメ見る時間が惜しいですし）。
各装備も「広範囲低火力高サイクル」、「万能寄りボム弱め」、「高火力範囲中低サイクル」「ドリル」とバラエティに飛んでおり、その何れも用途を心得ていれば実に爽快な使い心地です。
音楽も古典ロボットへのリスペクトに満ちており、聴き応え十分。こんなにティンパニ鳴らしてるゲームBGMってそう無いんじゃなかろうか。
更に、ボス前に登場する博士が色々とアレで。彼のトークはウィング無しのロケットパンチプレイで読めますので、一度低難易度ででもお試しください。
総じて、スーパーロボアニメが好きなら是非。ノーマルなSTGファンにもおすすめの一本です。

I grew up on Voltes V and Getter Robo, so this is wonderfully nostalgic to me. Supercharged Robot VULKAISER is as simple as shmups get; screen scrolls, enemies shoot, you shoot back while dodging projectiles. There aren't any massively impressive gimmicks here or anything new to the genre. There are no power-ups, you only get the chance to "Combine" your mecha to different forms throughout each level. Levels are simple and straightforward, with one mini-boss and a stage boss. You've seen it all before and you'll see it again.

I'm recommending it purely for the theme. It is designed to look and sound like those 1970s mecha anime shows. There is no story per se, but it is about a team of five color-coded pilots, each with their own vehicle, who Vulkaiser can gattai with to gain different abilities.  Each level starts with a card reminiscent of an episode title card and ends with a piece of dialogue /advice from the last team member you were combined with. The music is instant nostalgia-train to the face, if you've ever watched those shows back in the '70s-'80s.

Not that gameplay isn't good, mind you; it's simple, but it works perfectly. Enemy projectiles are clean and obvious, Vulkaiser's hitbox is small (and the game points directly to it), controls are tight, the different mecha configurations add a layer of strategy (however basic) to the game. 

The game does offer different difficulty levels to play around with, which is good, but from now on I'm docking points from any shmup that doesn't have a proper "training" mode on PC. That 1CC should be a goal, not a punishment. Perhaps I'm just mis-remembering things, but the appeal of the arcade experience when I was a kid didn't revolve around running out of quarters and crying into my milkshake. 

That aside and much as I enjoy this little thing, I *would* recommend picking it up on a sale. It's surprisingly effective as a nostalgia trip and it's fun to play, but 5-ish bucks are too much for a fairly short shmup that doesn't add a whole lot to the genre. Pick it up for three during a sale; two bucks might sound like an insignificant price difference, but these are two bucks you can invest in another Astro Port shmup; because these guys make pretty good stuff, in all of their simplicity.

Vulkaiser é um shmup que superou minhas expectativas.

O jogador tem uma barra de vida e mais a da nave auxiliar que efetuar a fusão. Não tem escolha a priori de naves, o jogador controla a Vulkaiser, e no decorrer dos levels aparecem naves para fazer fusões, cada uma com uma habilidade diferente. O ataque é apenas em 1 botão. Segurando solta o especial, que assim como o estilo do tiro, varia conforme a fusão. As cenas de final de fase variam conforme o personagem selecionado. E se acabada uma fase com a nave auxiliar destruída, ela não aparecerá novamente para fazer fusões.

Vulkaiser really captures the Saturday morning Super Robot feel. The game follows a 'quick to learn, tough to master' format. You essentially will have to 1-credit-clear the whole game (which makes sense, since there can be only one SUPERCHARGED ROBOT VULKAISER!) which is where a lot of the difficulty in the game comes from. There are 5 different modes, including the base mode, that act as sporadic power-ups for Vulkaiser as you progress through the levels. The recurring General mini-boss fights are quite enjoyable and the game has a very charming sense of humor about it; an homage to the Super Robot genre and anime in general. I'm struggling to beat arcade mode on normal difficulty, but there are two more additional difficulties if you are a supreme SHMUP player and want a real challenge. I love this dev and picked this title up as part of the Astro Saga, in case you want to save some money and buy all the (excellent) games from this dev.
